Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Miami FL
752 AM EDT Thu Aug 27 2026

...New AVIATION...

.KEY MESSAGES...
Updated at 748 AM EDT Thu Aug 27 2026

 - Scattered showers will develop through the early evening hours,
   with coverage most likely across interior and Southwest FL. 
   Heavy rain, frequent lightning and gusty winds will be possible
   with the stronger storms.

 - High temperatures will continue to peak in the low to mid 90s 
   each afternoon through the rest of the week.

&&

.SHORT TERM...
(Today through Friday)
Issued at 254 AM EDT Thu Aug 27 2026

The wet, unsettled pattern will continue for the rest of the week as 
South FL remains flanked by two blocks of upper level ridging over 
the southeast US and over the western Atlantic. Heights across 
the peninsula will remain a bit lower than the surrounding 
features thanks to the simultaneous influences of an upper level 
trough over the Ohio River Valley, and several subtle TUTTs 
approaching from the Caribbean. This setup will continue to 
promote moisture advection across the area, and more widespread 
convection each afternoon. Forecast soundings continue to show a 
moist atmospheric column, with PWATs back up to 2 inches or more 
across much of the area. With ample instability in place (in 
excess of 2500 J/kg), 500mb temperatures that are trending lower 
than they have over the past several weeks (down to -7C to -8C), 
and DCAPE values exceeding 700- 800 J/kg, storms will have no 
difficulty developing along the sea breeze boundaries each 
afternoon. And, given the forecast parameter space, some stronger 
storms could end up producing wind gusts 40-55 mph and small hail.
Additionally, given the surge in moisture HREF guidance suggests 
1-2 inches could fall across portion of the interior and 
southwest FL, with isolated 3-4 inches in some spots. Similarly to
previous days, activity is most likely to start developing across
the East Coast where the sea breeze moves in, then propagate 
inland into the late afternoon and evening hours, where coverage 
will be maximized. 

Temperatures will continue to peak in the low to mid 90s each 
afternoon. Heat indices will linger in the low 100s, but cloud 
coverage associated with storm activity should help mitigate values 
rising into the 105-110F range. That being said, today's chances for 
heat indices to rise above that range are slightly higher than the 
last couple of days given the potential of convection not firing up 
until after noon. Thus, short-fuse Heat Advisory could be needed 
later today if this other solution pans out. Overnight temperatures 
will also remain fairly balmy, with lows in the upper 70s to low 80s 
across the East Coast, and down to the mid 70s across the
interior. 

&&

.LONG TERM...
(Friday night through Wednesday)
Issued at 254 AM EDT Thu Aug 27 2026

Conditions will remain wet and unsettled through the extended period 
as the previously discussed pattern remains in place through the 
weekend. During this time, the upper level trough over the eastern 
US will deepen southward, with an associated front settling over the 
southeastern US. Easterly to southeasterly flow will continue across 
our region, with PWATs continuing to trend near normal or slightly 
above normal (1.9-2.1 inch range). Each afternoon could bring 
scattered to numerous showers and storms, starting along the East 
coast sea breeze boundary then proceeding inland into the late 
afternoon hours. Similarly to the short term period, gusty winds, 
heavy rainfall and frequent lightning will all remain possible 
hazards.

Starting next week, once the trough and front progress eastward, 
models start to suggest the two flanking ridges over the US and 
western Atlantic will start to merge, extending across the entire 
region. Afternoon showers and thunderstorms will remain likely each 
afternoon, with coverage maximized across the interior and southwest 
FL thanks to the continuing easterly flow. 

Temperatures through the period will remain seasonably hot, with 
highs in the low to mid 90s each afternoon and overnight lows in the 
low 80s across the coastlines, and mid 70s over the interior. 

&&

.AVIATION...
(12Z TAFS)
Issued at 748 AM EDT Thu Aug 27 2026

L/V winds will enhance out of an onshore component (SErly along
the east coast, SWrly at KAPF) between 16-18z. SHRA/TSRA is
forecast to develop by 17-19z with a maxima of coverage mainly
across inland portions of South Florida. While confidence for
terminal impacts remains low, sub-MVFR cigs/vis as well as gusty
winds is possible at any terminal that is impacted by SHRA/TSRA.
L/V winds and a return to dry and VFR conditions is forecast
overnight once residual daytime SHRA/TSRA dissipates.

&&

.MARINE...
Issued at 254 AM EDT Thu Aug 27 2026

Benign boating conditions will prevail across all local waters as 
light to moderate winds continue. Across the local Atlantic waters, 
easterly to southeasterly winds will prevail, while westerly 
winds are forecast over the local Gulf waters. Scattered showers 
and storms are expected each day, mainly in the morning hours and 
again in the late evening hours across the local waters. Locally 
hazardous winds and rough seas may occur near any storm.

&&

.PRELIMINARY POINT TEMPS/POPS...
Miami            92  79  92  80 /  40  20  30  30 
West Kendall     92  77  92  78 /  50  20  40  30 
Opa-Locka        93  79  93  80 /  50  20  30  30 
Homestead        92  79  92  80 /  40  20  30  30 
Fort Lauderdale  91  79  91  80 /  40  20  30  30 
N Ft Lauderdale  92  80  92  81 /  40  20  30  20 
Pembroke Pines   91  79  92  81 /  50  20  30  30 
West Palm Beach  92  78  93  79 /  50  20  40  20 
Boca Raton       90  78  90  80 /  40  20  40  20 
Naples           91  77  92  76 /  40  20  50  30 

&&

.MFL WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
FL...None.
AM...None.
GM...None.
&&

$$

SHORT TERM...ATV
LONG TERM....ATV
AVIATION...Hadi
